results.title: Riccy Mabel
results.overview: In 1991, 17-year-old Riccy Mabel leaves La Ceiba for Tegucigalpa to train as a teacher, then disappears. Reconstructing her case, the film follows the traces of devastating violence and the questions that remain when the truth emerges too late.

results.title: Atomic Eve
results.overview: In the year 2029, the world is at war. As announcements of incoming nuclear attack shake the United States, people of all walks of life scramble to reconcile with the end of the world.

results.title: One Night at KitKat
results.overview: Berlin, Saturday night. Behind the doors of the legendary KitKatClub, a world unfolds that usually remains hidden. In a place where mobile phones are strictly forbidden, a camera was allowed inside. The founding duo looks back on the origins of the club—a venue that, like few others, epitomizes Berlin’s club culture, techno, the fetish scene, and sex-positive parties. Guests and staff share stories of self-acceptance, body positivity, and community. Intimate, unfiltered, and non-judgmental, the documentary offers an exclusive glimpse into a night at the KitKat.

results.title: I feel something towards you
results.overview: Feeling something towards you, they write letters. Defying the texts that define their actions, they begin to act differently.

results.title: What to Say
results.overview: A crowd. A touch. Uncertainty. What now? Tereza finds herself in a room full of people, unsure of what to say, even though she feels so much inside. Words fail her, but her inner world is vivid and alive. Through a variety of textile materials, the film gives shape to her unspoken emotions and sensory experiences, transforming fabric into a language of its own. It is a story about the quiet struggle and gentle courage of searching for closeness.

results.title: The Echoes
results.overview: A short story about loss and memory, inspired by the forced resettlement of the Lemko community from the Carpathian Mountains.

results.title: Crowyokan
results.overview: Comedian Pandji Pragiwaksono turns spontaneous audience exchanges into an intimate and unpredictable crowd-work special.

results.title: Cam Girl
results.overview: CAM GIRL is a romance drama about four cam models at four very different points in their careers. It moves between the noise of the adult industry and the quiet, often lonely life on the other side of the camera.  Alana is a grocery store clerk in Medellín who can’t cover her grandfather’s medicine when her best friend Roxana tells her to try camming. Sally is a rising cam star in Cyprus, still grieving her father and losing herself in everything her new life can buy. Hope is a perfectionist who hides what she does from the man she’s falling for, hoping he’s the one thing she’s missing. Lexi is an industry icon pulled in every direction, shut off from the real world and from herself.  Their stories cross, and together they show what life as a cam girl actually looks like.

results.title: COLLIDEOSCOPE
results.overview: Filmed, edited and scored in ten days, COLLIDEOSCOPE is a non-narrative structural experiment consisting of ten 10 second chapters, each with ten overlays of shots that were filmed for the amount of time shown and without a second take. It acts as a capsule of misjudged, fleeting moments told in linear metaphors about the journey from life to death.

results.title: Middle of Nowhere
results.overview: Kakuma means "middle of nowhere." It's also where Mo Jabari is from, a refugee camp in Kenya where seasons were sandstorms and survival was not a metaphor. He arrived in Canada with nothing recognizable except men fighting on a television screen. Middle of Nowhere follows Mo Jabari through the unglamorous world of Canadian independent wrestling, no guarantees, no safety net, and no one coming to help if you get hurt today. In a business built on fabricated spectacle, Mo's answer is simple: "I don't have to be a gimmick. I just gotta be me."

results.title: Face to Face: Don Bachardy
results.overview: A revealing documentary that explores the vibrant life, work, and flamboyant personality of portrait artist Don Bachardy, focusing on his lifelong romantic partnership with novelist Christopher Isherwood. From their Santa Monica home, Bachardy spills vivid details on his sitters: how he got to touch Ginger Rogers' face, how Henry Fonda—who famously hated queers—eventually came around to pose for him, and how Governor Jerry Brown actually sat for his portrait 40 years ago, unlike Ronnie and Arnold. Bachardy's unique philosophy allows him to enter his sitters' lives, discern their personalities, and see straight into their souls. Yet, the emotional core and pinnacle of the documentary is his profound bond with Isherwood. During Isherwood's final six months, as he lay bedridden and dying right in front of him, Bachardy produced 448 black-paint portraits. Explaining that his paintbrush was in mourning, Bachardy offers a breathtaking, devastatingly pure expression of love and loss.

results.title: Eight Heels and a Hard Truth
results.original_title: Eight Heels and a Hard Truth
results.overview: Set in the Southeast—where LGBTQIA+ histories have long been under-documented—Eight Heels and a Hard Truth follows a Mexican-born trans woman who survived silence, violence, and erasure in the Deep South’s bail bond world before reclaiming her voice and joining other leaders in Atlanta. The film honors the resilience of trans women like her who not only survived, but thrived as “ladies” in the South—often unseen, but never without power.

results.title: Beyond the Doors of Club 708
results.overview: A poignant short documentary that explores the legacy of an iconic venue in Atlanta's Black LGBTQ+ community. Once a vibrant hub for connection and celebration, the club's sudden closure left a significant void in the lives of its patrons. Through archival footage and personal testimonials, the film chronicles the rich history of Club 708, reflecting on its cultural impact and the community's resilience in the face of loss. This documentary not only captures the essence of what the club represented but also imagines the possibilities of what could have been, highlighting the ongoing need for safe spaces in the community.
